title: The man who slept seventy years

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? who are the people who really know you, the ones you’d call if something big happened?
options: then hold them close today. listen.
sometimes one is a whole world. listen.
I’m not sure I have anyone
i’m really glad you’re here. listen, this one is for you.

steps.line: The Talmud tells of Honi, a holy man. One day he saw an old man planting a carob tree. “How long until it gives fruit?” he asked. “Seventy years.”
“Will you live seventy years?” The old man said, “I found carob trees in the world. As my ancestors planted for me, I plant for my children.”
Honi sat down to eat, and sleep came over him. Rocks rose up around him, hiding him from view, and he slept for seventy years.

steps.q: Honi wakes after seventy years. What does he see first?
o: Someone picking fruit from the carob tree
steps.why: A man gathering carobs: the planter’s grandson.

steps.line: When he woke, a man was picking carobs from the tree. “Did you plant this?” Honi asked. “No, my grandfather did.”
Honi went to the study hall. He heard the scholars say, “These teachings are as clear as in the days of Honi.” “I am Honi!” he said. No one believed him.

steps.q: The scholars praised Honi’s teaching to his face, not knowing it was him. Why was that no comfort?
o: He wanted credit for his teachings
Admired isn’t the same as known
He feared they had twisted his words
steps.why: His teachings were alive, but no one knew him. The Talmud says they didn’t give him the honor due, and it broke his heart.

steps.line: Heartbroken, Honi prayed for mercy, and his life came to an end. That, the Talmud says, is the old saying: either friendship, or death.

steps.q: In Aramaic the saying is “o chavruta, o mituta.” What is a chavruta to Jews today?
steps.why: Chavruta comes from chaver, friend. Jews still learn in pairs, arguing out loud, because life alone goes dim.

steps.q: Honi is famous for another Talmud story too. What was he called?
steps.why: In a drought he drew a circle in the dust and said he wouldn’t step out until God sent rain. The rain came.

steps.line: Today, Jews often study in pairs. A study partner is a chavruta, the very word in Honi’s saying. You learn together, out loud, arguing and laughing.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the first thing the torah calls “not good” isn’t a sin. it’s loneliness: “it is not good that the man should be alone.”
and the partner god makes is an ezer kenegdo, a help facing him. ezer is a word the bible also uses for god. it’s not a junior word. it means someone who can look you in the eye.

steps.q: Honi had his name, his teachings, even his fame. From his story, what does a person most need?
o: To be remembered after they’re gone
People who know them, face to face
steps.why: People who know you, face to face. That’s the help the Torah means: someone facing you.

today.say: today, ask one person to learn something with you: a chapter, a recipe, a song. that’s chavruta, friendship out loud. or simply call someone who really knows you.
options: then you’ll have a chavruta. honi would be glad.
one call. it isn’t good to be alone, so don’t be.

tomorrow.title: Where are you?
tomorrow.line: two people hide in a garden, and god asks the first question in the torah. long after, a rabbi in a prison cell explains why.
